Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Ms. Nushra Siddiqui Advocate holding brief of Ms. Anjali Singh Tomer, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
155 of 2022, under Sections 2/3 U.P. Gangsters Act, Police Station Civil Lines, District Aligarh,
during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text: Police Station Civil Lines, District Aligarh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Applicant was made accused in the present case on the basis of solitary case of murder shown against him in the gang chart.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is neither member nor leader of any gang and he never indulged in any anti-social activity.

5. She further submitted that however on the basis of solitary case of murder shown in the gang chart, applicant was made accused in the present matter but in that case, after considering entire facts of the case, this Court, enlarged him on bail.

6. She further submitted that apart from the present case and solitary case shown in the gang chart,

7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submitted that in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 10.6.2022 i.e. for almost two years.
8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the factual arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. From the perusal of the record, it appears that however on the basis of solitary case of murder shown in the gang chart, applicant was made accused in the present matter but in that case, after considering entire facts of the case, this Court, enlarged him on bail.

11. Further, however, apart from the present case and solitary case shown in the gang chart,
applicant is having criminal history of a case of sections 376 and 377 IPC but it appears that this case arose due to matrimonial dispute and in that case also applicant has been enlarged on bail even by the court concerned.
12. Further, applicant is in jail in the present matter since 10.6.2022 i.e. for almost two years.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Ankush Agarwal, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
